newsitem.title: USA: US corporate bonds firm led by Morgan, Ford issues.
newsitem.headline: US corporate bonds firm led by Morgan, Ford issues.

text.p: U.S. corporate bonds spreads were bolstered by gains in some hefty new issues on Monday and closed flat to firmer in a mostly quiet session, dealers said.
Corporate issuers Korea Development Bank and Bear Stearns Cos Inc also capitalized on vibrant market tone with the sale of large debt offerings.

In the secondary, the $1.0 billion Morgan Stanley Group 10-year note deal of Friday saw powerful followthrough demand when freed, traders said. The issue, already priced at a tight 57 basis points over the Treasury curve, tightened to a 54 basis point bid, 52 basis point offer in moderate trade.

Ford Motor Credit Corp's $1.25 billion five-year global notes also traded higher. The notes were seen bid at 37-1/2 bid, 36 offer near the close compared with its issued spread of 38 basis points, a trader said.
Other investment grade spreads were unchanged to tighter in an otherwise dull session, traders said.

New issues included a $300 million CPI-linked A1/AA-minus five-year issue from Korea Development Bank via J.P. Morgan Securities, priced at 3.4 percentage points over CPI. The first ever inflation indexed Yankee bond was sold to insurance companies, money managers and pension funds, J.P. Morgan said.

Also on Monday, Bear Stearns Cos Inc issued $350 million A2/single-A 10-year notes as 7s to yield 68 basis points over the Treasury curve. The issue priced at the wider side of price talk but was also increased in size from the $300 million size thrown about earlier in the session.
Bear, Stearns & Co Inc was lead manager on the deal.
Turning to high-yielders, traders reported a mostly quiet session but stressed the cash-infusion into mutual funds would continue to outpace supply. Some spreads were firmer.
Active on Monday were Revlon Worldwide's 12 percent senior secured discount notes of 1998, traders said.

The soon-to-be defeased notes were firm but little changed at 93 to 93-1/2 bid, according to several traders. The debt will be defeased through a $500 million issue of new zero coupon bonds and a capital infusion from MacAndrews & Forbes Holdings Inc, sources said.
Approximately $100 million of the debt traded between Friday and Monday's session, one trader said.

Elsewhere, Penn Traffic Cos 9-5/8s doubled gains of Friday and closed at a bid of 46. The debt, which had been banished to the mid-30s on a string of poor earnings, realized gains of more than four points on Monday, traders said.
Gains were attributed to talk of a management change, bargain hunting and short covering.
New high-yield issues were topped by $120 million 9-1/2 percent B3/B-minus senior subordinated notes from The Fonda Group Inc, priced at par to yield 310 basis points over the Treasury curve.
Bear, Stearns & Co was the lead manager on the deal.

Like the mass majority of high-yield issues of late, the issue was increased in size (from $110 million) and traded up more than one point upon removal of syndicate restrictions, syndicate sources said.

U.S. Treasuries closed lower with Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony looming on Wednesday, analysts there said. The benchmark 30-year bond closed down 7/32 to yield 6.66 percent.
